pairs.difference: A: no single hero. A cluster of four pumpkins with leaves and vines sits mid-card, the fence crosses behind it and grass tufts fill the foreground, so the thumbnail reads as a little scene. B: one topiary stands on a plinth, tall and clear, with a hedge and path kept behind it. Numbers are in range for both, so this rests on the eye, and B's setting is also fairly full.
pairs.fix: One big pumpkin as the only subject, filling most of the card and slightly cropped by the bottom edge; no fence, no extra small pumpkins, plain soft background.

pairs.difference: B: the lion and its wide plinth run nearly edge to edge (width 0.935, margin 0.026, area 0.444, just over the real maximum). The winding path, trees and bright lawn behind it compete with the pale statue at thumbnail size. A: the red cooler sits slightly left of centre, with its open lid breaking upward, on a calm beach. The red block reads first and the background stays quiet.
pairs.fix: Show the lion alone on a low base, closer in, against a simple soft green or blue backdrop; remove the winding path and the trees.

pairs.difference: A: the bat is a thin horizontal band, wingtips almost touching both sides (width 0.949, above real) while height is only 0.371 (real minimum 0.581). Area 0.181 is also below real. The small dark body sits in the middle with large empty rings above and below. B: the tilted envelope with photos is a compact mass that fills the card (area 0.428) and reads at once.
pairs.fix: Draw the bat bigger and closer with wings raised and folded up around the body, so it fills the card top to bottom; tilt it slightly on a diagonal.

pairs.difference: B: the cauldron faces dead-on, centred and symmetrical on a flat ledge, with an even gap around it (margin 0.126, above real maximum). A static placement, like the generated lessons. A: the shoes sit in a three-quarter view with a diagonal run, close to the left and right edges (margin 0.033, at the real floor). A has its own fault: height 0.487 is below real, leaving the top third empty, so the call is weak.
pairs.fix: Turn the cauldron to a three-quarter view from slightly above, make it larger so it nearly touches the side edges, and tilt it a little off centre.

pairs.difference: B: the candelabra is complete, upright and mirror-symmetrical, centred with its base floating above the bottom edge. Thin arms leave a low mass (area 0.183) and the flames are small accents. A: the lamp is off-centre with its curved arm to one side, and the post is cropped by the bottom edge like the real lighthouse lesson, pushing the lantern large and close. A's area is also low, but its crop reads as real framing.
pairs.fix: Move in close so the candle holder is cropped by the bottom edge, make the candles and flames much larger, and turn it slightly off-axis so it is not perfectly symmetrical.

pairs.difference: B: the whole house is shown on its own hill, centred with sky around it, and it runs almost the full height (0.942, above real; margin 0.002). Windows, turret and roofs are many small, equal accents, the complete-object-plus-ground habit of the generated lessons. A: a tight crop on the door, cut by the top and bottom edges, with the wreath as a clear focus. A's area of 0.081 measures only the wreath, so that number does not count against it.
pairs.fix: Crop in on the front of the house so the roof and hill run off the card edges, keep one large glowing door or window as the focus, and remove the separate hill.

pairs.difference: A: the tombstone leans and reads instantly, but it sits on a neat mound of soil, stones and grass tufts inside a complete ground patch. That is the added-base habit seen in the generated lighthouse lessons. B: the slide is a looping structure cropped by the pool and deck at the bottom, a harder read but framed like the real roller coaster card. Numbers do not separate them.
pairs.fix: Enlarge the tombstone so its base is cropped by the bottom edge; remove the stones and the soil mound, keeping only a simple strip of grass.

pairs.difference: A: the crystal ball is dead-centre, frontal and symmetrical on a flat ledge, with equal air on both sides (margin 0.110, just above real maximum). B: the vending machine is turned three-quarters and stands slightly right of centre, showing its side, with a tall mass close to the top and bottom. B looks more like the placed objects on the real sheet.
pairs.fix: Tilt the view so the ball sits off-centre at a slight angle, make it larger so it nearly touches the card edges, and drop the flat ledge for a simple background.

pairs.difference: B: the broom is a thin diagonal stick and only the head at lower left has mass, so area 0.112 is far below the real minimum of 0.233 and most of the card is empty wall and floor. A: the mower is also low (0.209), with thin handles, but its red body and wheels form a large block that reads first. The diagonal in B resembles the real spyglass, but the spyglass has far more mass.
pairs.fix: Draw a much thicker, shorter broom with a large, wide bristle head filling the lower half of the card; make the handle chunky and let it run out of the top corner.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin is a large diagonal block, close to the left edge and reading at once. B: the chair is three-quarter view, with its top right finial near the corner. All measures are in range and both use the wall-and-floor split with a tilted, large hero. Composition gives no reason to choose.

A: the pumpkin is a nearly centred round mass, upright and frontal, with an even ring of space (margin 0.131, above real maximum of 0.116). It reads instantly but is static. B: the jacket spreads wider with sleeves near the sides, tilted by the diagonal sash, and its margin is in range. The call rests mainly on A's even, centred air.
pairs.fix: Make the pumpkin bigger and closer so it nearly touches the side edges, tilt it and turn it three-quarters, and shift it slightly off centre.

pairs.difference: A: the towel lies on a tilted diagonal, with a corner close to the left edge (width 0.923, slightly above real 0.896). B: the coral cluster sits centred on its rocks, in range, and framed much like the real coral on the reference sheet. Both have clear first reads and quiet backgrounds, and one slight width excess is no finding.

pattern: Generated cards show the complete object, upright and nearly centred, often frontal and symmetrical, with even space around it or a small added ground patch. Real cards commit harder: bottom-edge crops, tilts, three-quarter turns and offsets. Weak generated cards also lose mass, with thin stick or wing shapes that span the card but fill little of it (bat, broom, candelabra). Busy settings can also compete with the hero. Measured margin above about 0.11 or area below about 0.2 supports these reads, but most pairs are only weakly separated on composition.
